issue.title: New settings page listing upcoming booking reminders
issue.body:
Harness test (new screen). Add a new page under Settings where users see the reminder emails scheduled for their upcoming bookings (booking title, attendee, send time), read-only. Empty state when there are none.

Details from @lucasgrocha (comment 6756289657):
1. Compute the send time with a fixed rule: 24 hours before the booking start. No new scheduler or schema change.
2. Organizer only: bookings where the user is the host.

pm.summary: New read-only Settings page listing reminder emails for the host's upcoming bookings, send time fixed at 24h before start. This is a new screen, so it goes to the Designer next.
acceptance_criteria: A new page is reachable from the Settings navigation, with a clear title such as 'Booking reminders'.
The page lists one row per upcoming booking where the logged-in user is the organizer/host, showing booking title, attendee, and send time.
Send time equals the booking start time minus exactly 24 hours, shown in the user's timezone and locale format.
Bookings where the user is only an attendee are not listed.
Cancelled, rejected and past bookings are not listed.
Reminders whose computed send time is already in the past are still listed only if the booking is upcoming (decision: show them as is, no special state).
Rows are ordered by send time ascending.
When there are no matching bookings, an empty state with explanatory text is shown.
The page is read-only: no buttons or forms to edit, send or cancel reminders.
A logged-out user cannot access the page or its data; one user never sees another user's bookings.
No scheduler, database schema or migration changes are introduced.
All user-visible strings are in the English locale file.
Tests cover the 24h computation, host-only filtering and the empty state.

research.summary: Research done: settings pages are server page.tsx plus a client view, nav lives in SettingsLayoutAppDirClient. Data must be fetched without packages/trpc, which is out of scope. Next: PM decides, then the plan.
relevant_files: apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx (nav items; my_account list with appearance/out_of_office entries around lines 62-75)
apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/developer/webhooks/[id]/page.tsx (server page that reads data through a repository and prisma directly, no trpc)
packages/features/bookings/repositories/BookingRepository.ts (human-review area: read only; query shape with BookingStatus.ACCEPTED, userId, attendees)
packages/lib/dateTimeFormatter.ts (locale and timezone formatting helper) and packages/lib/dateTimeFormatter.test.ts (test style)
packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json (add strings such as booking_reminders, description, empty state, column labels)
patterns: New page = server page.tsx (generateMetadata via _generateMetadata, getServerSession check, redirect to /auth/login when logged out) rendering a client view from apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/*-view.tsx, imported as ~/settings/my-account/...
Nav entry: add an item with name (i18n key), href and trackingMetadata {section: "my_account", page: ...} to SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx
Views wrap content in SettingsHeader (title, description, borderInShellHeader) and use useLocale() t(...) for every string

Constraint: packages/trpc is outside the allowed scope, so a trpc router is not an option. Fetch in the server page via a prisma query or a small helper in packages/features/ or packages/lib/, and pass props to the client view. Server-side session scoping gives the user isolation.

Avoid putting new files in the human-review prefixes packages/features/auth/, packages/lib/server/ and packages/features/bookings/lib/. Adding a method to BookingRepository.ts is also in the review area (bookings/repositories is not listed, but it is the natural place), so prefer a new file under packages/features/settings/ or a new feature folder.
Pure helper, e.g. computeReminderSendTime(start) = start minus 24h via dayjs or Date arithmetic, kept separate so it is unit-testable

Query filter: userId = session user (organizer only), status ACCEPTED (maybe also PENDING; PM said not cancelled or rejected), startTime > now, order by startTime asc. This implies send time ascending since the offset is constant. Select title, startTime, and attendees' name/email.
Format the send time with the user's timeZone and locale (dateTimeFormatter or Intl); get them from the user profile (timeZone, locale) or the session

Tests are colocated *.test.ts or *.test.tsx. Vitest workspace includes packages/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}, apps/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,js}, apps/web/modules/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx and packages/features/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx. Use .test.tsx for view/empty-state tests under apps/web/modules/ or packages/features/, and .test.ts for pure logic. Mock prisma for the host-only filter test.

design_need.summary: This is a new Settings screen, so design is needed. The Designer gets a brief for a read-only list of upcoming booking reminders with an empty state, then the plan follows.
design_need.design_brief:
Design a new read-only Settings page, "Booking reminders", reachable from the Settings navigation (My account group).

Purpose: a host sees which reminder emails are scheduled for their upcoming bookings. Send time is always 24 hours before the booking start.

Reuse the existing Settings patterns: the same header (title plus short description), the same list and empty-state styling as other settings pages (e.g. out of office), and the same navigation item style.

Content per row: booking title, attendee (name and email), send time (date and time in the user's timezone and locale). Rows are sorted by send time ascending. Only bookings where the user is the host are shown.

Please specify:
1. Page title and description copy.
2. List layout (table or stacked rows), column labels, and how it behaves on mobile (narrow width).
3. Handling of multiple attendees on one booking and of long titles or emails.
4. Empty state: icon, heading and explanatory text, with no call to action that edits anything.
5. Navigation label and position within Settings.
6. Loading is not a concern (server-rendered), but note any skeleton if you see fit.

Constraints: no buttons, forms or actions to edit, send or cancel reminders. Light and dark themes must work using existing UI components. All strings must be i18n-ready (English keys). Past-due send times for still-upcoming bookings are shown as normal rows, with no special state.

Deliver: a layout description or wireframe of the populated state and the empty state, the component list from the existing UI kit, and the final copy strings.

plan.summary: Plan: a read-only "Booking reminders" settings page. A server page queries the host's upcoming bookings through prisma and passes rows to a client table view. A pure helper sets send time to start minus 24h. Needs plan approval.
files: apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(settings-layout)/my-account/booking-reminders/page.tsx (new: generateMetadata, session check, redirect to /auth/login?callbackUrl=..., fetch, render view)
apps/web/modules/settings/my-account/booking-reminders-view.tsx (new client view: SettingsHeader, responsive table, EmptyScreen, +N attendees Badge/Tooltip)
packages/features/settings/bookingReminders/getUpcomingBookingReminders.ts (new prisma query, userId = host, upcoming, ACCEPTED/PENDING, ordered by startTime asc, maps to rows with sendTime)

tests.purpose: Send time is exactly 24h before start, including across a DST boundary and month boundaries.
With prisma mocked, asserts the where clause: userId is the host, startTime > now, cancelled and rejected excluded, orderBy startTime asc. Also checks row mapping.
Empty state renders with its text and no controls. Populated rows show title, attendee and a formatted send time in the user's timezone, with no buttons or forms.

acceptance_criteria: Settings nav under My account has a 'Booking reminders' entry linking to /settings/my-account/booking-reminders.
The page lists one row per upcoming booking where the user is the host, with title, attendee and send time.
Send time is start minus exactly 24h, shown in the user's timezone and locale format.
Attendee-only, cancelled, rejected and past bookings are excluded. Rows are ordered by send time ascending.
Past send times for upcoming bookings are listed as is.
The empty state shows its explanatory text when there are no rows.
The page is read-only: no buttons or forms.
Logged-out users are redirected to login. The query is scoped to the session user id.
No scheduler, schema, migration or packages/trpc changes.
All strings come from en/common.json.
The new tests pass with TZ=UTC yarn vitest run, and yarn type-check and yarn lint pass.
steps: Add computeReminderSendTime.ts using Date arithmetic (start.getTime() - 24*3600*1000) and its unit test.

Add getUpcomingBookingReminders.ts using prisma directly: where {userId, startTime: {gt: now}, status in [ACCEPTED, PENDING]}, select id, title, startTime, attendees {name, email}, orderBy startTime asc. Map to rows with sendTime. Its test mocks prisma. Add to the new feature folder only, not BookingRepository.ts, to avoid the human-review area.
Add the en/common.json keys from the design: booking_reminders, _description, _column_booking, _column_attendee, _column_send_time, _empty_title, _empty_description, _load_error, _more_attendees.

Build booking-reminders-view.tsx as a client component (props: rows, timeZone, locale) following out-of-office-view and the selected design: SettingsHeader, real table with sr-only caption, th scope=col, time dateTime, stacked rows below sm, EmptyScreen with BellIcon and no CTA, +N Badge with Tooltip for extra attendees. Format send time with Intl or dateTimeFormatter. Add the view test.

Add the page.tsx following the appearance page: getServerSession with buildLegacyRequest, redirect to login when there is no session, read the user's timeZone and locale, call the query, and render the view. Add _generateMetadata. A fetch failure goes to the Next error boundary.
Add the nav item in SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx with trackingMetadata {section: 'my_account', page: 'booking_reminders'}.
Run TZ=UTC yarn vitest run on the three new tests, then yarn type-check and yarn lint.
open_questions: Should PENDING (unconfirmed) bookings be listed along with ACCEPTED? The plan assumes yes, since the PM only excluded cancelled and rejected.
Is the optional loading.tsx skeleton wanted? The plan leaves it out to keep the change small.

evaluation.summary: Plan fits scope and the selected design, but test coverage has gaps (redirect, rendered ordering, status filter) and the files list has duplicates. Revise these, then confirm the PENDING assumption.
missing_acceptance_criteria: Logged-out redirect / no data access has no test (only stated in the plan criteria, no page test)
Rows ordered by send time ascending is only asserted via the orderBy clause in the mocked query test, not on rendered rows
Attendee-only exclusion is covered only by the where clause (userId = host); no explicit test of attendee-only exclusion beyond that
Nav entry 'Booking reminders' has no test
Past-send-time rows listed as is has no explicit test
All strings in en/common.json is verified only by review, not by a test
Attendee shown as 'Name +N' with multiple attendees is not tested
findings: Files list repeats the three test paths at the end (duplicates); clean up so each file appears once.
All planned files are inside the allowed prefixes and extensions; none touch human_review prefixes or apps/web/proxy.ts. Avoiding BookingRepository.ts and packages/trpc is correct.

Plan assumes PENDING bookings are listed (open question). PM only excluded cancelled and rejected, so this is a reasonable reading, but the test should assert the status filter explicitly (ACCEPTED and PENDING in, CANCELLED/REJECTED out), not just 'excluded'. Confirm with the PM or owner.

The where clause uses status in [ACCEPTED, PENDING]; PM text says 'cancelled and rejected not listed', and the test purpose should match that. Consider whether other statuses (e.g. AWAITING_HOST) exist; the allow-list could silently drop them.

Query test mocks prisma and asserts where/orderBy, which covers the host-only filter and 24h mapping at the data layer. The page-level session check (redirect, userId from session) is untested; add a small test or explicitly justify the gap.

The 24h computation uses fixed-millisecond arithmetic, which is correct for 'exactly 24 hours'. The DST test case should assert absolute instants (not wall-clock), as the displayed local time can differ by an hour across DST. State this in the test purpose.

Design is followed: responsive table, sr-only caption, th scope=col, time dateTime, EmptyScreen without CTA, +N Badge with Tooltip, no interactive controls. Design copy keys are listed in full. The load_error key is added but the plan routes errors to the Next error boundary, so the key may be unused; either use the Alert or drop the key.
Optional loading.tsx is left out, which is fine since the design marks it optional.
Ensure the query caps or limits results is not mentioned; consider a take limit to avoid unbounded rows (not in the PM criteria, so optional).

Page lives under packages/features/settings/ for the query helper, which is allowed. Because the apps/web page imports prisma data directly, confirm that the repo's lint rules do not forbid prisma use in apps/web or require the repository pattern.
